definition_of_universal: A single objectively specified nonzero covariant cosmic vorticity or cross-sector field generator with identifiable, independently testable predictions; not mere ubiquity of local rotational structures.

evidence.claim: SO(2) plane rotation and norm preservation
evidence.description: Rigid rotations preserve Euclidean norm; a mathematical theorem, not a measurement of the cosmos.
evidence.limits: Requires a specified action on a plane and an angle, no universal parameter.

evidence.claim: In 3-D the fixed-axis generator squares to minus transverse projection, not minus 3-D identity
evidence.description: The representation has a fixed axis, and this is why naive 2-D rotor generalization needs a domain.
evidence.limits: No assertion that the physical universe selects an axis.

evidence.claim: Curl of a C² real scalar gradient vanishes
evidence.description: A smoothly differentiable single-valued real scalar does not have intrinsic ordinary vorticity.
evidence.limits: Multi-valued phases and zeros require punctured-domain treatment.

evidence.claim: Rigid rotation field has curl equal to twice angular velocity
evidence.description: v=(-ωy,ωx,0) yields curl v=(0,0,2ω).
evidence.limits: Applies to the explicitly defined rigid flow.

evidence.claim: A real scalar can be constant in space and time
evidence.description: φ=C is nonrotating; disproves the literal claim that every scalar has nonzero gradient vorticity.
evidence.limits: Does not rule out hidden coupled fields under an additional model.

evidence.claim: Complex phase ψ=ρ exp(iθ) admits integer winding around nodal defects
evidence.description: If ψ is nonzero on a closed loop, its continuous phase change is 2πn, n integer.
evidence.limits: Topological winding is not automatically a mechanical angular velocity; gauge-invariant circulation needs the connection.

evidence.claim: Madelung phase current is conventional hydrodynamic structure
evidence.description: Monolithic 102 has one-space/one-time mathematical specializations of phase current and conserved current.
evidence.limits: The full relativistic/curved extension and observed universal phase are not shown.

evidence.claim: Zero amplitude invalidates a global smooth phase angle
evidence.description: At ψ=0 the phase is undefined, so global phase coordinates need patching/topological data.
evidence.limits: Finite winding can exist around punctures but cannot be promoted to global smooth θ.

evidence.claim: Vorticity and circulation characterize local rotational flow
evidence.description: Curl u, circulation and stretching are defined for differentiable flows; each flow may or may not be rotational.
evidence.limits: Irrotational flows are permitted, including pure-gradient potential flows.

evidence.claim: Quantized vortices observed in dilute-gas Bose-Einstein condensates
evidence.description: Interference phase maps and stirred-condensate experiments demonstrate vortices and angular momentum.
evidence.limits: Prepared laboratory systems; not evidence of rotating spacetime everywhere.

evidence.claim: ME-077–082 introduce thixotropic/variable-viscosity constitutive relations
evidence.description: Model includes time-dependent η and continuity; special cases reduce to ordinary incompressible NS under extra assumptions.
evidence.limits: ME-078 has η(0)=0; does not prove uniform positive viscosity or general NS regularity.

evidence.claim: BSA-R Step 7 explicitly leaves cone-integrability estimate open
evidence.description: Conditional direction-coherence machinery does not establish an a priori Kξ estimate for every smooth 3-D flow.
evidence.limits: No resolved Millennium problem is inferred.

evidence.claim: Neutron interferometry supports the spin-1/2 4π rotational behavior
evidence.description: Observed coherent sign change is consistent with spinor double-cover geometry.
evidence.limits: Spinor representation is not classical rotation of the entire universe.

evidence.claim: Earth's frame dragging measured by Gravity Probe B
evidence.description: Published geodetic and frame-dragging gyroscope results agree with GR within uncertainty.
evidence.limits: Earth's angular momentum generates a local dragging effect; does not identify cosmic bulk rotation.

evidence.claim: LIGO GW150914 observations infer a spinning final merger remnant
evidence.description: Binary merger gravitational-wave event and modeling constrain a rotating astrophysical object.
evidence.limits: Does not imply primordial common cosmic spin; component spins were not well resolved in this event.

evidence.claim: Faraday/polarization rotation inferred near M87*
evidence.description: Polarized emission and Faraday effects probe magnetic fields and plasma near black hole.
evidence.limits: Polarization-angle rotation is not evidence of metric vorticity on Hubble scales.

evidence.claim: Physically coupled Bianchi VIIh rotation tightly constrained by Planck
evidence.description: No evidence for physical Bianchi VIIh model; (ω/H)₀<7.6e-10 at 95% confidence in the specified analysis.
evidence.limits: Do not apply the numerical bound to all rotating geometries; decoupled Bianchi fits are cosmologically inconsistent.

evidence.claim: 2015 Planck nonphysical decoupled Bianchi fit is not a physical rotating-universe detection
evidence.description: An improved temperature fit in an inconsistent decoupled model is not evidence for a self-consistent cosmology.
evidence.limits: Distinguish model comparison and parameter coherence.

evidence.claim: JADES galaxy-handedness imbalance reported in 2025
evidence.description: A peer-reviewed analysis reports unequal projected spin handedness in one observed deep-field sample.
evidence.limits: Selection, recognition bias, viewing geometry, redshift and hemispheric replication remain alternative explanations; not a measurement of metric rotation.

evidence.claim: Anisotropic cosmic birefringence remains constrained
evidence.description: A 2025 CMB B-mode analysis reports amplitude consistent with zero within 2σ and a model-dependent bound.
evidence.limits: Polarization rotation/axion couplings are not the same observable as metric vorticity.

evidence.claim: Rotating Newtonian-universe simulations are theoretical
evidence.description: Exploration of shear-free or global-vorticity Newtonian models; a model family to test, not measurement.
evidence.limits: Newtonian global rotation is not a covariant Einstein-metric derivation.

evidence.claim: ME-055 defines universal rotation using curl of a proposed cosmic velocity field
evidence.description: Ω_U=∇×v_U requires a physically defined v_U and a cosmological congruence.
evidence.limits: No observed nonzero cosmic v_U or invariant vorticity detection.

evidence.claim: ME-056 adds a scalar Ω²/a² term to Friedmann-like rate equation
evidence.description: An explicitly stipulated scalar extension, not a derived Einstein/Bianchi model.
evidence.limits: Need metric, stress-energy, units, dynamical evolution and data; strong k−ω² degeneracy.

evidence.claim: ME-056 scalar sign and curvature degeneracies are established within chosen equation
evidence.description: ω and −ω give the same rate; k−ω² is what scalar expansion constrains.
evidence.limits: A single H(a) observable cannot uniquely measure ω without independent constraints.

evidence.claim: ME-055/056 rigid rotation normalization is vorticity=2 angular speed
evidence.description: If ω denotes rigid angular speed, a term in ω² equals |curl v|²/4.
evidence.limits: The chosen identification of cosmic parameter with local rigid rotation is additional modeling.

evidence.claim: There is no verified identical nonzero rotation generator coupling all field sectors
evidence.description: Cross-sector universality is a hypothesis requiring an action, coupling, invariants and a distinctive observable prediction.
evidence.limits: Analogies between spin, phase, polarization and vorticity do not establish a common physical origin.

evidence.claim: Exact 1+3 Gauss scalar includes shear, projected rest curvature, and a negative bare vorticity-square contribution
evidence.description: 3H² = kappa*rho+Lambda+sigma²−omega²−R_rest/2, with definitions and signature fixed; it does not imply a standalone positive Omega_U²/a² correction.
evidence.limits: Projected rest curvature is not a global hypersurface Ricci scalar for rotating congruences. Different assumptions or metric-dependent curvature can change the net correction.

evidence.claim: Gödel exact Einstein dust spacetime rotates without expanding
evidence.description: Independent pinned SymPy verification yields the historical Gödel Einstein tensor, theta=0, shear=0, omega²=m²/2>0, and negative Lambda.
evidence.limits: The Gödel spacetime has closed timelike curves and is not the observed universe. This refutes rotation⇒expansion generally, not every restricted EFMW cosmological model.

evidence.claim: ME-056 requires an additional shear/curvature compatibility condition to match covariant Einstein cosmology
evidence.description: Necessary condition: 3 Omega_U²/a² = sigma²−omega²−(R_rest−6k/a²)/2 when rho, Lambda and measured H coincide.
evidence.limits: A scalar algebraic identity does not supply a spacetime metric, matter conservation, geometric definitions of a/k/Omega_U, or a valid Einstein solution.
